acceptance: Downloader/verifier disambiguates attempts (latest-wins) or failed-attempt artifacts are namespaced/cleaned automatically; no manual deletion required
context: Merged as PR 3272 (3125c0428). The medium-collection, medium-shard and coverage-map evidence uploads in ci.yml, trunk.yml, trunk-coverage.yml and test.yml now set overwrite: true (actions/upload-artifact v6.0.0: a matching artifact is deleted before the new one uploads), so a rerun replaces the failed attempt's evidence instead of leaving two same-named artifacts for the download pattern to merge. tests/unit/workflows/test_evidence_artifact_reruns.py requires overwrite: true on every SHA-keyed evidence upload; with the workflow change removed all 9 uploads fail it. Not yet observed on GitHub: the replacement happens inside upload-artifact on a real rerun. Check the next rerun of a failed medium shard (artifact list of the run should show one artifact per name); if two still appear, the verifier needs an attempt-aware lookup and this item should reopen.
description: CI run 38267710571 accumulated three same-named t2-medium-shard-0-d05f41116 artifacts (IDs 11757022181 exit 1, 11762606819 exit 1, 11762303564 exit 0). The core aggregator (release_canary_sharding.py verify-medium exact-assignment check) kept failing on the stale exit-1 evidence after the shard reran green. Resolved by manually deleting the two stale artifacts via the API and rerunning core, which passed. Manual artifact deletion is a destructive workaround, not a process.
